config.title: Reusable Button

intro.title: Reusable Button
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Button component in React. You'll learn how to create a component that accepts props to customize its text and appearance, making it flexible for use across different parts of an application. The core concept is component reusability, which allows you to write efficient, maintainable code by avoiding duplication. You'll use JSX for structure, JavaScript functions to define the component, and props to pass data into it. By the end, you'll have a button that can be easily adapted with different labels and styles.
intro.usecase: Reusable buttons are foundational UI components found in nearly every web application. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon, consistent buttons handle 'Add to Cart', 'Buy Now', and 'Save for Later' actions across product pages. Dashboard applications like Salesforce use reusable buttons for 'Save', 'Submit', and 'Export' operations to maintain visual consistency. Form-heavy applications such as banking portals rely on reusable buttons for 'Transfer', 'Pay', and 'Cancel' actions to ensure predictable user interactions. This pattern allows developers to maintain consistent styling and behavior while reducing code duplication across complex interfaces.

objectives: Construct a reusable Button component with configurable props
Apply different styling patterns based on variant props
Initialize and manage state for interactive button behaviors
Bind event handlers to respond to user interactions
Integrate the reusable Button into multiple parent components
Manipulate button appearance dynamically using props
Render conditional content within the button based on props

steps.title: Import React
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file so you can use JSX and create components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React is imported and ready to use in your component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React. This allows you to use JSX syntax and create React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing React from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import React from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the Button component function
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Button that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called Button that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Create the Button component function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Button component function is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The Button function is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Button component function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named Button that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component function is not correctly defined. It should be named Button and return null.

steps.title: Add props parameter to Button
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to your Button component function so it can receive data from parent components.
steps.hint: Add parentheses after the function name and include the parameter 'props' inside them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will be able to receive props from its parent component.
successCriteria: The Button function has a props parameter in its parentheses.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Button component now accepts props, which is essential for making it reusable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the props parameter inside the parentheses of the Button function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component still doesn't have a props parameter. Add 'props' inside the parentheses after the function name.

steps.title: Add onClick handler prop
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, destructure an onClick prop from the props parameter.
steps.hint: Use object destructuring to extract onClick from props, like: const { onClick } = props;
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will have access to an onClick prop that can be used to handle click events.
successCriteria: The onClick prop is destructured from the props parameter in the Button component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully destructured the onClick prop, making it available for handling click events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're destructuring onClick from the props parameter inside the Button component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the destructuring syntax. You need to extract onClick from props inside the Button component.

steps.title: Add children prop for button text
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, destructure a children prop from the props parameter to make the button content customizable.
steps.hint: Add children to the destructuring statement alongside onClick. Then use {children} inside the button element instead of the hardcoded text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will accept children content through props and display it inside the button element.
successCriteria: The Button component destructures children from props and uses {children} as the button content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the children prop, making the button text customizable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you destructure children from props and use it inside the button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component still has hardcoded text. Destructure children from props and use it as the button content.

steps.title: Return button JSX element
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, return a button JSX element.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax to return a <button> element from the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component returns a button element.
successCriteria: Button component returns a <button> JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've returned a button element from the Button component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a <button> element from the Button component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component should return a button element using JSX syntax.

steps.title: Wire onClick prop to button
steps.instruction: In the Button component, add the onClick prop to the button element to trigger the handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Pass the onClick prop from the component's parameters to the button's onClick attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element will have an onClick attribute that calls the handler passed via props.
successCriteria: The button JSX includes onClick={onClick} (or onClick={props.onClick}) to connect the click handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've wired the onClick prop to the button, making it interactive.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button's onClick attribute is set to the onClick prop from the component's parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still needs the onClick prop to be connected. Add onClick={onClick} (or onClick={props.onClick}) to the button element.

steps.title: Display children prop as button content
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, replace the static text 'Click me' with the children prop to display dynamic button content.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} to embed the children prop value inside the button element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will display the text passed via the children prop instead of the hardcoded 'Click me'.
successCriteria: The button element renders the children prop value between its tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The button now displays dynamic content through the children prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the children prop inside the button tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still shows 'Click me'. Replace it with the children prop.

steps.title: Export the Button component
steps.instruction: Make the Button component available for use in other files by adding a default export statement.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component is exported as the default export of this module.
successCriteria: The Button component is exported as a default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Button component is now exported and can be imported and used in other files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct export syntax: 'export default Button'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is not exported. Use 'export default Button' to make it available.

steps.title: Test the Button component
steps.instruction: Import the Button component and use it in your app with different text and click handlers to verify it works.
steps.hint: Import Button from './Button' (or the correct path) and add multiple Button instances with different children and onClick props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component is imported and used with different text and click handlers, demonstrating its reusability.
successCriteria: Button is imported and used at least twice with different children and onClick props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the reusable Button component with different props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure to import Button and use it multiple times with different children and onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is not properly imported or used with varied props. Review the import and usage steps.
